text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.

LONDON - Britain's leading share index powered to a record closing high as investors overlooked the strength in sterling to focus on fresh takeover speculation, a surge in pharmaceutical stocks and a bumper sale by chemicals giant ICI. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,857.4, up 57.9 points, or 1.21 percent.

FRANKFURT - Shares look set to continue to pursue a relentlessly upward course as long as the dollar underscores their rally but dealers were uncertain how long the U.S. currency's support can last. The DAX-30 index closed at 4,124.19, up 83.22 points, or 2.06 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 4,142.19, up 67.89 points, or 1.67 percent.
PARIS - The French stock market was closed for the Bastille Day holiday. It will reopen on Tuesday.

ZURICH - Shares put an end to last week's three-day correction and closed higher, buoyed by firmer pharmaceutical shares. The SMI rose 44.3 points or 0.76 percent to 5,845.8 after hitting a day's high at 5,892.7 points.

MILAN - Shares closed below record highs, as European bond markets came off the boil, after a strong performance in which banks did much of the running. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 14,068, up 50 points, or 0.36 percent.
AMSTERDAM - Shares spiralled to another record close, with the dollar's strength opening the way up as soon as the session started. The AEX index closed at 948.17, up 11.66 points, or 1.25 percent.

TOKYO - The stock market's key Nikkei 225 index climbed back above 20,000 as investors, including pension funds, actively sought high-technology issues backed by firm earnings, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,228.72, up 353.23 points, or 1.78 percent.

HONG KONG - Banking stocks led a broad rally in share prices, with the Hang Seng Index hitting a record high in morning trade before ending the day off its peaks but at a record close as property stocks succumbed to profit-taking. The Hang Seng index closed at 15,370.94, up 145.65 points, or 0.96 percent.

SYDNEY - A thinly traded share market tumbled to a lower close with bewildered brokers searching for reasons after upbeat offshore finishes had promised much more. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,673.0, down 26.1 points, or 0.97 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares finished strongly up, buoyed by a higher bullion price, but profit-taking before the close dragged major indices off their highs. The All-share index closed at 7,380.6, up 32.6 points, or 0.44 percent. The All Gold index closed at 999.6, up 34.8 points, or 0.41 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 8,842.5, up 35.9 points, or 3.61 percent.
